source_review.notes: Checked every structured reference for identity, date or edition, and cited scope. Mokhov, Mitchell, and Peyton Jones support the separation of dependency model, scheduler, and rebuilder. Current GNU Make official documentation supports dependency-correct parallel execution, finite job slots, recursive jobserver coordination, and token return on errors. Current GitHub Actions documentation supports distinct matrix, max-parallel, fail-fast, and continue-on-error controls. Current GitLab official guidance supports explicit needs-based DAG execution rather than broad stage barriers. Current Bazel documentation supports remote parallel action execution and its execution-environment requirements. Verified CLRS fourth-edition metadata and the Lamport CACM paper identity and DOI for durable foundations. Checked 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined DAG vertices and edges, duration, start and finish times, work, span, makespan, resource demand and capacity vectors, worker eligibility, speedup, efficiency, and shard sets before formal use.
Checked summation, maximum, path, set, union, intersection, inequality, and componentwise vector notation and every GitHub math delimiter.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All claims state the identical-worker, deterministic-duration, acyclic-workload assumptions where those assumptions matter.

evidence: Recomputed the four-job model: work 13, critical paths 11 and 7, two-worker lower bound 11, legal schedule makespan 11, and serial-relative speedup 13/11 = 1.18 after rounding.
Recomputed greedy shard placement for weights 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, and 4 as three bins of 13.
Checked the second exercise independently: work 14, span 12, two-worker lower bound 12, and schedule A 0-3, B 3-8, C 3-5, D 8-12.
Executed ci-parallelism-model under CPython 3.14.4 and matched eight exact output lines with empty stderr and exit status zero.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Durations are deterministic teaching inputs, not measurements of a real CI fleet.

evidence: Derived work conservation pT_p >= W and precedence-path bound T_p >= S, then combined them as T_p >= max(W/p,S).
Checked average-parallelism ratio W/S and qualified it as a model ceiling rather than an achieved worker count.
Checked speedup W/T_p and efficiency W/(pT_p) only for identical work and comparable setup and cache conditions.
Checked shard completeness as union equal to U with pairwise-empty intersections and explicitly qualified intentional replication.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No approximation ratio, queueing theorem, or universal scalability claim is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed empty readiness, cyclic graphs, missing dependencies, broad barriers, zero useful parallelism, critical-path domination, heterogeneous placement, scarce licenses, unavailable platforms, nested oversubscription, and worker loss.

Reviewed new and slow tests, stale estimates, skewed shards, missing and duplicate items, mutable manifests, exclusive databases, fixed ports, shared workspaces, cache writers, and cross-candidate artifact collision.

Reviewed fail-fast and collect-all policy, cancellation, cleanup, retry classification, preemption, starvation, burst queues, noisy neighbors, remote transfer domination, untrusted code, and secret-bearing runners.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Production admission must use measured demands, trust boundaries, and workload-specific failure semantics.

evidence: Traced frozen candidate and workload identity through selection, precedence, admission, placement, execution, artifact transfer, and aggregation.
Checked readiness decrements each predecessor edge exactly once and capacity reservations are acquired atomically and returned exactly once.
Checked shard aggregation rejects missing, unexpected, conflicting duplicate, wrong-candidate, and wrong-plan results.
Checked cancelled, unavailable, failed, lost, timed-out, and completed states remain distinct and no incomplete state is represented as pass.
invariant_checking.notes: Correct scheduling cannot compensate for an incomplete selected workload or an undeclared dependency.

evidence: Reviewed the work bound from finite worker-time and the span bound from non-overlap on one precedence path; both premises are used in the combined lower bound.
Reviewed readiness correctness via frozen indegrees and exactly-once predecessor completion processing.
Reviewed capacity conservation through atomic vector reservation and exactly-once release, including lost-worker reconciliation.
Reviewed shard completeness from exact comparison of accepted item identities against the frozen universe.
proof_review.notes: The arguments establish properties of the stated models, not optimality of every list schedule or correctness of any vendor CI service.

evidence: Audited uses of proof, lower bound, optimal, complete, independent, correct, safe, exact, deterministic, available, and verified.

Confirmed the chapter labels the lower-bound proof, shard-completeness argument, executable model assumptions, hypothetical cases, current official product behavior, and professional policy separately.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Only the two numerical DAG examples are shown optimal because their legal schedules attain proved lower bounds.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet under CPython 3.14.4 with the declared exact output, empty stderr, and exit status zero.
Confirmed deterministic work, span, lower bound, makespan, speedup, shard balance, memory rejection, and conservative fallback output.
Confirmed all fleet, queue, runner, test-duration, failure, remote-execution, and cost scenarios are explicitly pedagogical rather than reported production measurements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real CI provider, runner fleet, remote executor, queue, build, test suite, or artifact service was benchmarked.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the full chain from frozen selected workload through DAG precedence, work/span limits, ready scheduling, multidimensional admission, placement, nested budgets, matrices and shards, mutable-state isolation, failure policy, queueing, and end-to-end measurement. Selection, scheduling, admission, and placement remain distinct concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed failures across stage barriers, missing edges, resource mismatch, scarce pools, platform unavailability, nested oversubscription, skewed or stale shard plans, new tests, lost workers, shared databases and ports, artifact collision, incomplete aggregation, cancellation, retries, starvation, transfer overhead, trust zones, and fleet-level contention. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified undergraduate progression from precise vocabulary through the work/span model and proofs, one executable eight-outcome scheduler model, resource and sharding mechanisms, eight explicit trade-off pairs, eighteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked situations, and five exercises progressing from definitions through derivation, diagnosis, evidence-system design, and unfamiliar investment choice.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Sources, abstract scheduling bounds, deterministic examples, hypothetical cases, and one local model execution do not establish dependency completeness, scheduler optimality, resource isolation, shard validity, test adequacy, artifact integrity, CI service reliability, production speedup, fleet throughput, or cost reduction.
